message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.17","text":"And I set out my purpose from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries, and everything that I disclosed to you at the outset, so that I may not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to travel with you—for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire. But first I want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul proves to be mortal or is immortal; whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here; whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world came into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist.” And, to avoid speaking item by item, I said that I wanted to learn these things and those that follow from them.\n\nIn reply he said, “I will briefly give you knowledge of the things that exist, Clement; for the present, hear from that knowledge.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς ζητήσεις ἀπόρους ἐκενώθην","chosen":"I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries","rationale":"The passive form of κενόω is figurative here: the inquiries had left the speaker spent or emptied, while ἄπορος describes questions offering no way through."},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο γὰρ οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως χαίρων θέλω","chosen":"for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire","rationale":"The rendering preserves the parenthetical uncertainty of οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως and the positive force of χαίρων θέλω; alternatively, the phrase may mean “for somehow—I do not know how—I gladly desire this.”"},{"source_quote":"περὶ ἀληθείας πρῶτον πληροφορηθῆναι","chosen":"first I want to be fully assured about the truth","rationale":"πληροφορέω denotes being brought to full assurance or certainty, not merely receiving information."},{"source_quote":"καὶ εἰ ἀίδιος οὖσα περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι","chosen":"whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here","rationale":"The main rendering takes ἀίδιος οὖσα conditionally because the preceding question leaves the soul’s immortality unsettled. The participle can alternatively state the circumstance or premise: “whether, being eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here.” This is an interpretive ambiguity rather than source corruption."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι","chosen":"it is to be judged for what it has done here","rationale":"ἔχει with the infinitive expresses what is appointed or bound to occur; the feminine subject remains the soul."},{"source_quote":"εἴ τι ποτ᾿ ἔστιν δίκαιον ἢ ἀρέσκον θεῷ","chosen":"whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God","rationale":"τι ποτε asks whether any such thing exists at all, while both adjectives remain coordinated."},{"source_quote":"καὶ εἰ κρείττων ἔσται ἢ οὐδὲ ἔσται","chosen":"and whether it will be better or will not even exist","rationale":"οὐδέ supplies emphatic negation: the alternative to the world being better is that it will not even exist, not merely that it will no longer exist."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω","chosen":"to avoid speaking item by item","rationale":"κατ᾿ εἶδος can mean by individual form, category, or particular item; the context abbreviates a longer enumeration."},{"source_quote":"τὰ νῦν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἄκουσον","chosen":"for the present, hear from that knowledge","rationale":"τὰ νῦν is temporal, while αὐτῆς most naturally refers back to the promised knowledge; “hear the present points from it” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
